transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Elaine Carter (Orion VP AI), Martin Ruiz (Head Infra), Sofia Alvarez (ML Eng)
---
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for making time, i'm Samir from Redwood, i run enterprise for the west region. quick intros?
[00:08] Elaine: hi, i'm elaine, vp of ai for the consortium, we coordinate models across a few research labs, nice to meet you.
[00:13] Martin: martin here, infra lead, i'll be focused on network, vpc and k8s concerns.
[00:18] Sofia: sofia, ml eng, i'll be running the benchmarks and evals.
[00:22] Maya: maya here, solutions engineer, i'll pair with samir on the technicals.
[00:28] Samir: great. quick agenda, we want to understand your current stack, goals, and then talk model selection — open models, context length, multilingual, tool calling — and discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private. does that sound right?
[00:38] Elaine: yep that's perfect. our immediate problem: we have a multi-lab knowledge ingestion pipeline and need an assistant that can handle 60-100k tokens for long docs, and must support english, spanish, french, and japanese at high quality. also tool-calling to hit internal databases and run small compute.
[00:56] Sofia: and we need this to be reproducible, so model versioning and deterministic outputs-ish matter for some workflows.
[01:04] Maya: ok, good, that helps. can you share a bit about current infra — where models run today?
[01:10] Elaine: currently we use a mix — some in-house endpoints using open-source weights on k8s, some hosted APIs from public clouds for prototypes. infra is primarily on GCP with private peering for some partners. our blockers have been latency at scale and unpredictability of cost.
[01:26] Martin: also, data residency - certain labs required EU-only. and for some datasets we need to use customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS).
[01:34] Samir: totally — we see that a lot. on model selection: for 64k+ context you generally look at models that are optimized for long context or where you can use Redwood's prefix/KV caching and efficient kernel selection. the open model landscape is varied — people mention Llama-2 variants, Mistral, Mistral-instruct forks, and the newer long-context models like LongLLaMA or models fine-tuned with efficient attention.
[01:55] Sofia: we've looked at some forks but worried about perf and memory. what does redwood provide out of the box for long context?
[02:02] Maya: our runtime does continuous KV cache and smart chunking, plus compilation choices for attention kernels. practically that means we can serve 64k contexts with lower cost than a naive full attention run, but hardware matters — >=H100 or equivalent for best throughput. also we have recommended quantization profiles.
[02:23] Martin: hardware wise, we're leaning towards dedicated capacity if throughput is a priority. can you explain tradeoffs hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[02:31] Samir: sure. hosted is fastest to pilot — lower setup, pay-as-you-go, good for multi-region prototypes. dedicated is reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput and isolation, better tail latency and cost at committed volume. private gives you customer-managed network, on-prem option and direct KMS/HSM control for compliance. tradeoff is time-to-deploy and operational ownership.
[02:52] Elaine: and in terms of model choices, are you recommending redwood-verified open models for this workload? we prefer open weights due to license flexibility.
[02:59] Maya: we maintain a model catalog with verified performance profiles — we can recommend candidates: a long-context tuned Llama variant, a Mistral 7B tuned for instruction, and a larger long-context open model for higher quality on multilingual tasks. each has latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.
[03:17] Sofia: multilingual quality is a big one — spanish/french ok but japanese tends to lag. what benchmarks do you have?
[03:23] Maya: we've run internal evals on our corpus — Japanese improves significantly with larger models or targeted finetunes. for cost-conscious tiers, a multilingual tuned 13B can give decent results; for best-in-class we recommend 70B long-context variants on dedicated hardware. we'll share relevant eval sheets.
[03:40] Martin: tool calling — we need model to call internal REST APIs and run simple compute securely. any limitations?
[03:45] Maya: we support structured tool-calling patterns and function-like APIs. for private deployments we can keep the control plane in the cloud while the model lives in your VPC, or run everything on-prem. network egress, auth to internal services, and secrets (KMS) are all common concerns we handle via connectors and service accounts.
[04:03] Elaine: can we orchestrate a flow where the model calls a data lookup service that sits behind our VPC?
[04:07] Maya: yes — typically we'd either set up a secure peering and ephemeral credentials or run a private deployment where the model has direct network access. Martin, that sounds like something you'd want to deep-dive.
[04:16] Martin: yep, let's do that. also curious about auditing — we need full audit logs and token-level usage attribution.
[04:21] Samir: Redwood Console exposes token breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and audit logs. for private deployments, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[04:29] Sofia: performance test — we'd like to run our prompt set across candidates. can you run a 48hr benchmark?
[04:34] Maya: we can. typical approach: run candidate models on dedicated infra with your prompt distribution, measure p95 latency, throughput, token cost, and output quality metrics. we'll need a sample prompt set and success criteria.
[04:46] Elaine: timeline — we want a pilot in Q3, production in Q4 if benchmarks are good.
[04:51] Samir: makes sense. can you spell out success criteria?
[04:54] Sofia: 1) acceptable Japanese F1/qa score compared to baseline, 2) p95 latency < 800ms for short calls, for long-context ops we accept higher as long as throughput is stable, 3) cost per 1k tokens not exceeding X (we'll provide target), 4) ability to call internal tools with secure auth.
[05:12] Maya: noted. on costs — long-context increases memory and token compute; dedicated commitments can lower unit cost significantly. we can model estimated per-token $ for your workload once we have prompt traces.
[05:24] Elaine: security — we need SOC2, ISO, SSO (saml), and KMS. do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:31] Samir: yes for private deployments and also for dedicated we offer integrations with major KMS providers and can support bring-your-own-key for certain tiers. we'll attach compliance pack.
[05:41] Martin: network question — do you support private peering to GCP?
[05:44] Maya: yes, peering and direct connect options exist; for on-prem we ship an appliance or air-gapped package.
[05:50] Elaine: about benchmarking — we'd like results of multilingual evals on the models you recommend.
[05:54] Maya: we'll include our internal evals and run your set as next step.
[05:58] Samir: any blockers we haven't covered?
[06:00] Sofia: licensing — some labs require permissive open licenses. we need clear SPDX-like info for any weights.
[06:06] Maya: we'll provide model license summaries and any caveats.
[06:10] Martin: also curious about rollouts — can you do canary deploys and A/B?
[06:14] Samir: yes, rollouts are supported: canary, A/B, and auto fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained.
[06:20] Elaine: great. let's recap next steps.
[06:23] Samir: recap: 1) Redwood to send Dedicated pricing and capacity tiers plus hosted comparison, 2) Maya to share SOC2/ISO/KMS and network docs, 3) run 48hr perf benchmark on 64k context with their prompt set (Maya + Sofia coordinate), 4) schedule infra deep dive for private deployment (Martin + Maya), 5) provide model license summaries and eval sheets.
[06:44] Elaine: that sounds right. target dates? we'd like benchmark in two weeks and infra deep dive next week if possible.
[06:51] Samir: we'll try to hit those. i'll follow up with a calendar invite and attach docs.
[06:55] Sofia: thanks everyone.
[06:57] Martin: thanks.
[06:58] Maya: thanks, bye.
[06:59] Samir: thanks all, bye.
---
Notes: transcription contains occasional minor mishears ("k v cache" for KV cache, "H one hundred" instead of H100 typed in auto transcript). References to external artifacts: "model-catalog-evals.xlsx" (will be shared), "security-pack.zip" (SOC2/ISO docs).
